rows.text: - M + 2H₂O → M(OH)₂ + H₂↑ (Ca, Sr, Ba) - Mg + H₂O(steam) → MgO + H₂ - 3M + N₂ → M₃N₂ - M + H₂ → MH₂ (CaH₂ = hydrolith) - IE₁: Be 899, Mg 738, Ca 590, Sr 550, Ba 503 kJ/mol - Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → BaSO₄↓ (white)

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Other Alkaline Earths Group IIA — Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Ra — carries two valence electrons and a different personality from Group IA: harder, denser, higher-melting, less reactive, and famous for **flame colours** and **sulphate solubility**. This topic is the trend table NEB asks as a 2–3 marker.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Electronic structure - General configuration [NG]ns²; oxidation state **+2 only** (Be²⁺ exceptional covalency). Removing the second s-electron costs more (second IE ~1800 kJ/mol) but the +2 lattice energies repay it — hence no +1 chemistry in solution.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Flame: brick-red Ca, crimson Sr, apple-green Ba; Be/Mg none. Sulphate ladder: Mg soluble -> Ba insoluble. mp: no trend in IIA. Be(OH)2 amphoteric. CaH2 = hydrolith.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Two electrons change the whole personality: the +2 lattice pays the second ionisation energy, so the metals are harder, denser and calmer than Group IA — and their sulphate solubility ladder becomes the analytical test that identifies sulphate everywhere.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Group IIA, [NG]ns2, +2 only. Down the group: radius up, IE1 down (Be 899 -> Ba 503 kJ/mol), density up (Mg dip 1.74), mp NO regular trend (Be 1287, Mg 650, Ca 842, Sr 777, Ba 727 C), reactivity up, electropositivity up. Water: Be none, Mg slow cold/brisk steam (MgO + H2), Ca brisk cold (Ca(OH)2 + H2), Sr/Ba vigorous.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Strontium's crimson flame is the red of emergency flares and fireworks; barium's apple-green colours the "green star" of every fireworks catalogue — the group's flame test written in the night sky.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): State the trend in the solubility of the sulphates of Group IIA metals and explain it.** — Solubility **decreases sharply down the group**: MgSO₄ is soluble, CaSO₄ sparingly soluble, SrSO₄ very sparingly soluble, and **BaSO₄ practically insoluble** (about 2.4 mg/L).…

Be and Mg have high ionisation energies (899, 738 kJ/mol) and small atoms whose excited states lie too high for Bunsen-flame energy — the electrons are not excited, so no emission.…  ·  ## 5. Common Confusions **Melting point has no monotonic trend here:** unlike IA (falling), IIA mp values zig-zag (Be 1287, Mg 650, Ca 842, Sr 777, Ba 727 °C) — quoting "decreases down" is wrong.  ·  **Be is the odd one:** amphoteric BeO/Be(OH)₂, covalent compounds, no flame colour — its tiny polarising ion makes it more like aluminium.
